newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul stocks end higher as Hanbo woes fizzle.
newsitem.headline: Seoul stocks end higher as Hanbo woes fizzle.

text.p: Stocks closed higher on Monday on the back of expectations of an early settlement to the Hanbo scandal and improving fundamentals, brokers said.
The composite index ended 9.57 points higher at 709.79.
"Effects of the Hanbo issue have been reflected. Liquidity remains ample and stock supplies in February and March are expected to be scanty," said Ha Man-yong of LG Securities.

Prosecutors summoned a close associate of President Kim Young-sam and two other politicians in connection with loans to Hanbo Steel Co. "Investigations seem to be focusing on political circles, and not on the business community," Ha said.
Volume totalled 29.31 million shares, compared with 34.13 million shares on Thursday. Advancers outpaced decliners 678 to 139 with 94 unchanged.
The market was closed on February 7-9 for the Lunar New Year holidays.
Brokers said stock supplies in February, including rights issues and initial public offerings, were estimated at 110 billion won against about 150 billion won in January.
The central bank said it supplied 1.26 trillion won to the banking system today through repurchase agreements to help banks meet their daily reserve levels.
"The money supply is a clear indication that the Bank of Korea has no plan to tighten money supply," said Lim Sung-woon of Daewoo Securities.

Late in the morning, the Ministry of Finance and Economy said the government would supply 1.4 trillion won to money markets this year to stop Hanbo Steel's financial failure from causing insolvencies at small companies.
"It seems safe to say the market is on the rise for the time being," said Kim Heung-shik of Hyundai Securities.
The March futures contracts rose 0.8 of a point to 73.60, while the KOSPI 200 index gained 0.78 of a point to 74.37.
